reflection:
Class Reflection: Designing Corporate-Startup Synergies (ENT 3805)

In our recent class discussions, we explored how corporations utilize open innovation to leverage external ideas and knowledge. Through various case studies, including P&G, LEGO, ISRO, and Philips, we analyzed the source and direction of innovation, as well as the value created for both the corporate and partner.

The class material emphasized the importance of understanding the different open innovation approaches, including the various sources of ideas and the direction of knowledge flow. For instance, P&G and LEGO used external ideas, while ISRO and Philips utilized internal sources.

To determine which open innovation approach to use, corporations must consider various factors, such as the source of the idea, the direction of knowledge flow, and the value created for both parties. By analyzing these factors, corporations can identify the most effective approach to achieve their goals.

One key takeaway from our discussion is that open innovation is not a one-size-fits-all solution. Corporations must carefully consider their specific needs and goals before selecting an open innovation approach. By doing so, they can maximize the value created for both themselves and their partners.

For future reference, I will keep in mind that open innovation approaches can vary in their source and direction of knowledge flow, and that corporations must carefully evaluate their options to achieve the best outcomes.
